title: security eng sync notes - 2026-03-22
content:
Security Engineering Sync — 2026-03-22
Attendees: Aisha Patel (sec eng), Marcus Chen (serving-runtime), Elena Rodriguez (platform eng), Devon Park (SRE), Samir Khan (product security), + optional: Jay (infra) joined for secrets split

Purpose: Weekly vuln triage, secrets detection status, threat-modeling follow-ups for Private/Dedicated deployments. Quick standup-style notes + action items. Doc is a working capture (notes to self style).

Agenda:
- Quick wins / updates
- Vulnerability triage: high/medium items from last 7 days
- Secrets detection: git leaks + pipeline blockers
- Threat modeling: private deployment network isolation & KMS integration
- Open questions / blockers / actions

1) Quick updates
- Marcus: runtime container CVE scan results — image-builder flagged libssl CVE-2026-1234 in one image tag used by canary. Patch PR ready (runtime:dockerfile#patch-ssl). Canary paused until image rotated.
- Elena: rolling creds rotation for dedicated pools — half complete for eu-west region; automation scripts fixed some edge cases.
- Devon: SLO incident last week caused by node OOM during a large-batch job; postmortem draft linked (JIRA-OPS-779). No evidence of exploit; resource exhaustion.
- Samir: customer reported scanning logs showing potential API key exposure in a customer-provided init script; triage in progress.

2) Vulnerability triage (prioritized)
- SEC-4678 (high): libssl CVE-2026-1234 in runtime base image (affects hosted & dedicated canaries). Impact: man-in-the-middle risk for internal mTLS if unpatched. Status: patch PR (#2345) by Marcus in review; build pipeline green for patched image. Action: deploy patched image to canary by 2026-03-23 09:00 PT. Owner: Marcus.
- SEC-4621 (medium): outdated tensorflow-serving wheel in a customer model-adapter image. Impact: low for majority, but two customers running custom adapters may be affected. Status: contact owners, create upgrade guidance. Action: Elena to raise docs + notify customers by 2026-03-24.
- SEC-4689 (low): linter reported weak crypto usage in telemetry collector (internal only). Plan: backlog item for Q2. Owner: Samir.

Notes: We confirmed CVSS score for SEC-4678 is 8.1 (high) based on ease of exploit + internal network exposure. No known active exploitation.

3) Secrets detection & pipeline blockers
- git-secrets run across monorepo yesterday: flagged 12 hits; 9 false positives (test keys), 3 true positives. Details: two historical commits with AWS access key (rotated), one accidental commit with a service account token used in a demo repo.
- Action taken: rotated the two AWS keys (done), rotated demo service account token (done), internal post-check: added additional prebake commit hook to catch base64 token patterns. Owner: Devon & Marcus.
- Pipeline blocker: pre-commit hook causing CI flakiness for windows runners — causing a number of PRs to fail transiently. Decision: temporarily relax strict hook on windows runners and enforce on linux. Devon to implement conditional hook by 2026-03-24.
- Secrets scanning coverage: still missing private-deployments repo and a few customer sandbox repos. Action: Samir to get allowlist from solutions-eng and schedule a scan for 2026-03-25.

4) Threat modeling follow-ups (private & dedicated deployments)
- Topic: KMS/HSM integration for Private installs — model artifact encryption at rest and in-transit. Current status: design doc exists (CONFLUENCE-SEC/threat-modeling-rt-runtime) but lacks clear L1/L2 keys separation and rotation policy.
  - Decision: define key hierarchy: root KMS (customer-controlled for private), service-level keys for runtime, and ephemeral session keys for cache. Samir to produce updated doc with recommended KMS policies by 2026-03-29.
  - Action: add requirement that Private installs must support HSM-backed keys for FedRAMP-targeted customers. Owner: Samir + Elena.
- Topic: Network isolation for dedicated GPU pools — discussion on whether to enable eBPF filtering at node level vs. VPC security groups. Notes:
  - eBPF gives finer-grained flow control and telemetry but increases kernel attack surface.
  - VPC level controls are coarser but simpler and aligned with current infra.
  - Action: Marcus to prototype eBPF policy for one dev pool (non-prod) and report perf/ops overhead by 2026-04-06. If positive, evaluate for gradual rollout.

5) Incident readiness / tabletop
- Plan tabletop for RCE in model-serving path (hypothetical exploit on a model-adapter). Target date: 2026-04-15. Responsible: Aisha to coordinate with SRE + Product.
- Prepare playbook steps for secrets-leak in public repos (rotate, notify, audit). Devon to update incident-runbook by 2026-03-28.

6) Open questions / blockers
- Should we enforce mandatory SOPS-encrypted config files for private deployments? Pros/cons discussed: encryption helps, but creates onboarding friction for smaller customers. Proposal: make it configurable but default-on for new private installs. Action: product security + product to finalize policy. Owner: Samir.
- How granular should role-based access be for console (token-level vs route-level)? Need product input. Action: Samir to schedule sync with product-hosted-api next week.

7) Action items (summary with owners & dates)
- Deploy patched runtime image to canary (SEC-4678) — Marcus — 2026-03-23
- Notify affected customers & publish upgrade guidance for TF wheel — Elena — 2026-03-24
- Implement conditional pre-commit hook for windows runners to reduce CI flakiness — Devon — 2026-03-24
- Rotate remaining keys and complete scan of private-deployments repos — Samir & Devon — 2026-03-25
- Update KMS/HSM key hierarchy doc + rotation policy — Samir & Elena — 2026-03-29
- Prototype eBPF policy on dev GPU pool — Marcus — 2026-04-06
- Tabletop for RCE scenario — Aisha to coordinate — 2026-04-15
- Update incident runbook for public repo leak — Devon — 2026-03-28

Notes / miscellaneous (informal):
- Remember to link runtime PR to GH issue and Jira ticket for audit trail.
- We should add a short checklist for new private deployments: "KMS configured, secrets scanning enabled, RBAC baseline applied". Could be a confluence template.
- Meeting cadence: keep weekly; next sync 2026-03-29.

End of notes.

Unresolved items / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm full list of repos excluded from git-secrets scanning (email solutions-eng).
- Confirm if canary SLA window allows short pause for image rotation (ops OK but check with sales for customer-facing impacts).
- Follow up on telemetry collector crypto rewrite timeline (move to backlog planning).

Attachments / links (inline):
- Runtime patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- CVE reference: CVE-2026-1234 (libssl)
- JIRA tickets: JIRA-SEC-4678, JIRA-SEC-4621, JIRA-OPS-779
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC/threat-modeling-rt-runtime

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (sec eng)
Reviewers: Marcus Chen, Elena Rodriguez, Devon Park
